subject: Maths
title: Histograms
subtitle: Statistics · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can draw and interpret histograms with equal and unequal class widths.

key_vocab.definition: A histogram displays continuous data using bars with no gaps. The frequency density is plotted on the y-axis when class widths are unequal.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can draw and interpret histograms with equal and unequal class widths.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: histogram -- A histogram displays continuous data using bars with no gaps. The frequency density is plotted on the y-axis when class widths are unequal.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Frequency density = frequency divided by class width. Area of bar = frequency.
Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width
Area of each bar gives the frequency for that class

Key examples:
  ✓ Freq density = 20 ÷ 5 = 4  (frequency 20, class width 5)
  ✓ Frequency = density × width  (area of bar = frequency)
  ✓ No gaps between bars  (data is continuous)
  ✗ Plot frequency on y-axis for unequal widths  (must use frequency density)
  ✗ Leave gaps between bars  (gaps are for bar charts, not histograms)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – calculating frequency density
  Class 10-20 has frequency 30. Find the frequency density.
  Class width = 20 - 10 = 10
  Frequency density = 30 ÷ 10
  = 3
  Frequency density = 3
  (Divide the frequency by the class width.)

Example 2 – finding frequency from a histogram
  A bar has height (density) 4 and width 5. Find the frequency.
  Frequency = density × width
  = 4 × 5
  = 20
  Frequency = 20
  (The area of the bar gives the frequency.)

sections.title: Calculating frequency density
sections.content:
Find the frequency density for each class.

(a) Class 0-10, frequency 25
(b) Class 10-30, frequency 60
(c) Class 30-50, frequency 44
(d) Class 50-80, frequency 90

sections.title: Finding frequency from density
sections.content:
Find the frequency (area of bar).

(a) Density 4, width 10
(b) Density 2.5, width 20
(c) Density 1.8, width 15
(d) Density 6, width 5

sections.title: Completing a table
sections.content:
Find the missing values.

(a) Class 0-5, freq ?, density 4
(b) Class 5-15, freq 30, density ?
(c) Class 15-25, freq ?, density 2.5
(d) Class 25-50, freq 75, density ?

sections.title: Interpreting histograms
sections.content:
Use the histogram data to answer.

(a) Total frequency if densities are 2, 3, 4 for widths 10, 10, 5?
(b) Which class has highest frequency: density 5 width 4, or density 3 width 8?
(c) Estimate median class if total freq = 60, first two classes have freq 15 and 25.
(d) Bar area = 36, width = 12. What is the height?

sections.title: Mixed histogram problems
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) Class 0-20 has density 1.5. Class 20-25 has density 6. Which has more data?
(b) Three classes: 0-10 (d=2), 10-20 (d=4), 20-50 (d=1). Total frequency?
(c) Frequency of 45 in class width 15. Density?
(d) Bar height 2.4, class 5-25. Frequency?
(e) Two bars: 0-10 (d=3), 10-40 (d=2). Estimate how many in 5-20.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width
✗ The height of a histogram bar always shows the frequency
✓ Histogram bars have no gaps because data is continuous
✗ Wider bars always represent more data
✓ The area of each bar represents the frequency
